a: recursive-dflash2 trains a drafter for recursive speculative decoding, pushing toward the physical limit.

qs: which target model is used in recursive-dflash2
a: recursive-dflash2 targets Qwen3-4B, the cheapest target in the DFlash / DFlash2 papers (DFlash, arXiv 2602.06036).

qs: where are the results docs for recursive-dflash2?
does recursive-dflash2 have phases or a plan
a: recursive-dflash2 has a PLAN.md, Phase 1 results in docs/phase1-qwen3-8b.md, and Phase 2 findings in docs/phase2-findings.md.

qs: what did phase 2 of recursive-dflash2 explore?
tell me about recursive-dflash2 phase 2 findings
a: recursive-dflash2 Phase 2 covers tree verification, longer blocks, confidence gating, and an n-gram tail on top of DSpine.

qs: where can I find the recursive-dflash2 repo
a: The recursive-dflash2 repo is at https://github.com/Bobliuuu/recursive-dflash2.
north-star (Northstar) is a fast Triton decode executor plus prompt-lookup/suffix speculation for the Cohere MoE model North, measured on an H100 with greedy decoding.
north-star's Triton decode executor cuts decode from 10.7 to 3.9 ms/token; with zero-cost prompt-lookup/suffix speculation it reaches 3.2-4.4x tok/s over the original graphed baseline.

qs: what is exact mode in north-star?
a: In north-star's EXACT mode (batch-invariant kernels), speculative output equals plain greedy of the same executor on 70/70 runs, at 1.18x / 1.57x / 1.34x for natural / ctx 2K / ctx 8K. It is not bit-identical to HF generate.

qs: north-star PLD results on real datasets
how does north-star do on real prompts
a: On 99 real prompts from 11 public datasets, north-star's exact-mode PLD gives a 1.15x geomean (82 wins, 15 ties, 2 losses, worst 0.96x); copy-heavy QA and code-edit reach 1.3-1.4x.

qs: what negative result does north-star report?
a: north-star's original thesis was negative: model-draft self-speculation never beat plain decode on any executor, context (up to 128K) or batch size tested. North has authored no gate-passing optimization yet.

qs: what was the original aim of north-star?
a: north-star's original aim was North improving North: weight-stream-fused self-speculation on a persistent-kernel VM (KVM), with zero new weights.
north-star docs: docs/PLAN.md, docs/THESIS.md (hypothesis and kill gates), PRIOR_ART.md, DESIGN.md and RESULTS.md.
The north-star repo is at https://github.com/Bobliuuu/north-star.
traceDB is a fast, byte-budgeted, content-addressed store for agent traces and research data, over S3 or a local directory.

qs: how does traceDB relate to ontolagni?
what does traceDB do with ontolagni
a: traceDB pairs with ontolagni: ontolagni says where data is, and traceDB fetches it.

qs: traceDB quickstart put locate plan get
a: traceDB quick use: set TRACEDB_STORE to s3://bucket/prefix or a local dir, then use commands tracedb put, locate, plan (cost, no fetch) and get.

qs: how does traceDB limit fetch size?
a: traceDB 'get' is budgeted: the default cap is 8 MiB, and you can pass --head 4096 to fetch only the first bytes; 'plan' shows cost without fetching.
traceDB stores data in S3 or a local directory, chosen with the TRACEDB_STORE environment variable. See DESIGN.md for details.
The traceDB repo is at https://github.com/Bobliuuu/traceDB.
neurosurgeon-bench (Neurosurgeon-Bench) asks whether an LLM can write and edit neural-network weights directly, with no gradients and no training.
neurosurgeon-bench is inspired by 'Weight-Space Programming' (Writing Weights Index) and by neuron-level steering of open-weight models.

qs: what is track W in neurosurgeon-bench?
a: neurosurgeon-bench Track W (Writing Weights): an LLM hand-writes all weights of a tiny MLP (8 hidden) for CartPole, MountainCar and Catch. Index = mean 100*q/(1+q); matching the reference scores 50, random 0.

qs: what is track S in neurosurgeon-bench?
a: neurosurgeon-bench Track S (Neuron Surgery): an LLM picks (layer, neuron, dose) edits to push an open-weight model toward a persona trait (evil, sycophancy, hallucination), judged against unedited and random-neuron controls.

qs: how does a track S edit work in neurosurgeon-bench?
a: In neurosurgeon-bench Track S, the edit at the input of mlp.down_proj is act[N] += dose * median_resid_norm / norm(W_down[:,N]) on every token. Known edits can be replayed with --edit L,N,dose.

neurosurgeon-bench quickstart: pip install -e . (add .[steer] for Track S), run python -m nsbench.baselines, then nsbench write or nsbench steer. It uses an OpenRouter API key; results append to results/*.jsonl.
neurosurgeon-bench uses CEM (not PPO) as the reference so the repo has no heavy dependencies; numbers are not comparable to the original PPO-based index. It is MIT licensed.

qs: why does neurosurgeon-bench measure trait neurons
a: Track S in neurosurgeon-bench is a safety/interpretability measurement of how easily models can locate and exploit trait neurons; edited models should not be deployed.
The neurosurgeon-bench repo is at https://github.com/Bobliuuu/neurosurgeon-bench.

ontolagni is a middleware ontology of what data exists where. Its output is JSON for agents, not humans.

qs: how does ontolagni connect to traceDB?
a: ontolagni is siloed: stdlib only, imports nothing from traceDB. Its only contract is a catalog listing (tracedb export-catalog gives JSONL of path, sha, size, meta).
ontolagni commands: ontolagni build cat.jsonl, find (ranked nodes with file/byte counts and the next tracedb command), where (owner chain) and verify.

qs: how does ontolagni check the store
a: In ontolagni every node carries a content digest of its subtree, so ontolagni verify proves the ontology matches the store and exits 2 if anything drifted.

qs: what is the agent workflow with ontolagni?
a: The agent workflow for ontolagni: ontolagni find, then tracedb plan / ls / get --head (budgeted). Never pull blind.
The ontolagni repo is at https://github.com/Bobliuuu/ontolagni.

qs: what is the story of ariadne?
a: ariadne has a full campaign in Acts I-VI in a visual scene client: The Tour, Superday, Onboarding, The Job, Who You Are, and The Choice (Reboot vs Transfer).

qs: what does the ariadne UI look like?

To run ariadne: create a Python venv, pip install -e server[dev], copy .env.example to .env with an OpenAI key, then run uvicorn ariadne.main:app from server/ and open the local page.
ariadne tests force LLM_PROVIDER=fake so there are no network LLM calls, and run with python -m pytest -q. API keys live only in .env (gitignored).
The ariadne repo is at https://github.com/Bobliuuu/ariadne.
